facts.text: Glenview Manor is a home rule-class city located in northern Jefferson County, about eight miles northeast of downtown Louisville.
Glenview Manor was formally incorporated in 1965, two decades before the original town of Glenview received similar recognition.
The name Glenview Manor comes from the nearby Glenview area, which was inspired by a historic trotting horse farm established in 1868.
Early settlers were drawn to the region's fertile soils and strategic position along the Ohio River bluffs during the late 18th century.
The Louisville, Harrods Creek, and Westport Railroad, completed in 1877, helped promote the area as a desirable retreat for the affluent.
Glenview Manor is one of the smallest incorporated municipalities in Kentucky, with a total land area of just 0.1 square miles.
